automated.evidence: Static, qualified-app, acceptance, SBOM, syntax, focused date/DST, IPC fixture, and independent review gates passed for the accepted runtime. Tagged CI repeats the complete current-Omarchy suite before drafting the release.

artifacts.evidence: The 0.1.2-rc.1 laptop archive passed the deterministic package-structure verifier and checksum verification; stable artifacts, checksums, SBOM, and attestations are reverified before publication.

install_upgrade_remove.evidence: Release owner restored the prior transactional installation, installed 0.1.2-rc.1 from the supplied local source archive on a current Omarchy laptop, and confirmed it is running correctly.

transactional_restore.evidence: The release owner exercised omacalendar-widgetctl restore followed by installation from the 0.1.2-rc.1 source; app widget activation tests cover isolated failure rollback and restoration.

views_edges.evidence: Headless Omarchy layout coverage remains in the tagged gate; the release owner accepted the running laptop candidate. Acceptance does not certify every physical display arrangement.

keyboard.evidence: Qt keyboard navigation, activation, and input-blocking tests are included in the complete tagged gate; the release owner accepted the laptop workflow.

real_mutations.evidence: The release owner accepted the running candidate against OmaCalendar 1.1.0; mutation-envelope and duplicate-submission fixtures cover create, update, move, remove, response, retry, and undo boundaries. Approval does not certify every provider scenario.

resilience.evidence: IPC fixtures cover fragmented and oversized input, malformed responses and snapshots, offline cache, daemon restart, revision gaps, sync-only changes, and incompatible protocol handling.

desktop_handoff.evidence: Native desktop handoff remains covered by the accepted 0.1.1 workflow and unchanged launch path; 0.1.2 adds stricter HTTPS meeting-link validation without changing app-link execution.

mixed_scale_theme.evidence: The tagged current-Omarchy gate repeats layout checks at 100%, 125%, and 200%; the release owner approved the laptop candidate. Physical mixed-monitor and theme combinations are not exhaustively certified.
